title: Transient Incident Credits & Auto-Reconciliation PRD
creator: Amira Patel
description: Problem: Customers sometimes experience brief service degradations or throttling events (e.g., regional capacity constraints, temporary model fallback, or routing incidents). Support currently issues manual goodwill credits after incidents, which is slow, inconsistent, and creates reconciliation overhead. This PRD proposes a system to automatically issue transient incident credits (TICs) to eligible customers during or immediately after a verified incident event, expose them in the Console and billing system as line items, and reconcile them automatically or surface them for manual review. Goals: 1) reduce time-to-credit and manual OPS/Sales work; 2) make crediting consistent, auditable, and easy to reconcile on invoices; 3) prevent double-crediting and limit financial exposure with caps and policies; 4) provide observable metrics for incident impact and crediting behavior.
business_rationale: Reduce manual toil: Support/Finance spends ~3–6 hours per high-touch incident issuing and reconciling credits.
Improve customer satisfaction by delivering faster remediation and transparent crediting.
Create predictable, auditable billing artifacts to simplify month-end reconciliation.
Enable product analytics to measure cost of incidents and ROI of reliability investments.
user_stories: As a customer admin, I want to see a temporary credit in my Console after an incident so I understand how my invoice will be affected.
As a support engineer, I want an automated credit applied for qualifying incidents so I don’t need to open manual billing tickets.
As a finance analyst, I want credits to be represented as distinct invoice line items with links to incident and audit records so reconciliation is straightforward.
As an SRE, I want the crediting trigger to tie directly to verified incident timelines (PagerDuty/incident timeline) to avoid subjective decisions.
requirements: R1: Incident detection integration - system must accept verified incident events from the incident platform (webhook payload from PagerDuty/Incidents service) including incident id, start/end timestamps, affected routes/tenants, severity.

R2: Eligibility rules engine - configurable rules determine which customers and which usage buckets (tokens, embeddings, dedicated capacity units) are eligible for TICs (e.g., paid customers only, exclude trial tiers).
R3: Credit calculation - automated calculation using configurable formulas: (affected_tokens * baseline_rate) * impact_multiplier capped at per-customer monthly cap. Support override by finance.
R4: Temporal scope - credits are transient (applied against the current billing period and zeroed/reconciled automatically in next invoice generation unless escalated to a permanent refund).
R5: Billing primitives - create invoice-ready line item entries: credit amount, reason code, linked incident id, metadata (trigger timestamp, rule id, applied_by=system).
R6: Audit trail - immutable audit entries for each TIC including inputs, rule match, calculation snapshot, and operator overrides.
R7: Console UX - new Billing > Credits view showing active TICs, pending auto-reconciliations, and ability for Finance to convert to manual refund or cancel.
R8: Notifications - automated notifications to tenant admin email and support when a TIC is applied with an explanation and link to Console view.
R9: API access - read-only endpoints for programmatic retrieval of TICs and a minimal write API for Finance to flag manual adjustments with justification.
R10: Safety controls - per-tenant monthly cap, per-incident cap, global monthly exposure threshold that requires Finance sign-off if exceeded.
out_of_scope: Automatic cash refunds (initial rollout will only apply invoice/credit line items; direct refunds via payment processor are manual).
Complex per-model quality adjustments (this PRD uses usage/latency/availability proxies only).
Retroactive credits beyond the active billing period unless escalated and approved by Finance.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Operational: Reduce manual credit tickets created by Support by 70% for qualifying incidents within Q2 post-launch.
Customer impact: Median time-to-credit <= 4 hours from incident resolution for automated TICs.
Financial: No more than 0.5% of monthly revenue credited via TICs under normal conditions (monitor for outliers).
Reliability: 100% auditability for TICs with incident link and rule id; zero incidents of silent/hidden credits in 3 months.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given a verified incident webhook (test fixture), the system applies TICs to all eligible tenants per rules and creates invoice-ready credit line items with incident id metadata.
AC2: Credits appear in the Console Billing > Credits list within 15 minutes of application and contain calculation details + link to incident timeline.
AC3: Finance can convert a TIC to a manual refund flag; converted credits produce an actionable ticket for payment team (integration placeholder OK for M1).
AC4: Credits are reconciled automatically at invoice generation (applied to outstanding charges) and are represented on invoice PDF/CSV as distinct line items with reason code and incident link.
AC5: System enforces per-tenant and per-incident caps; any credit that would exceed caps is truncated and a Finance alert is raised.
AC6: All TIC operations (auto-apply, overrides, cancellations) produce immutable audit logs accessible via the Console and Audit API.
AC7: End-to-end tests exist that simulate a multi-tenant incident, show correct credit math, UI visibility, and invoice generation with sample data.
billing_examples: Example A - Simple: Tenant A affected for 30 minutes, affected_tokens=120k, baseline_rate=$0.0004/token, impact_multiplier=0.5 => raw_credit = 120,000*$0.0004*0.5 = $24; applied_credit = min(raw_credit, per-incident-cap=$250) => $24 line item.

Example B - Cap enforcement: Tenant B raw_credit = $1,200 but per-tenant-monthly-cap=$500 and per-incident-cap=$300 => applied_credit = min(raw_credit, per-incident-cap) = $300; remaining cap for month = $200.
Example C - Multiple routes: Tenant C has two affected routes; credits calculated per-route then summed to a single TIC line item with per-route breakdown in metadata.
design_notes: Use existing billing line-item schema with an added 'credit_type=incident_transient' and 'incident_id' field to avoid schema churn.
Eligibility engine should reuse the entitlements/plan evaluation service to determine paid vs trial status.
Implement a lightweight rules DSL for impact multipliers and caps; v1 can be configured via Admin Console and persisted to Config Service.
Audit logs stored in ImmutableLog bucket with retention aligned to finance requirements (7 years) and surfaced via Audit API.
open_questions: Q1: What exact signals from the incident system qualify as 'verified' for automatic crediting? (SRE to propose mapping of incident severity -> verification thresholds).
Q2: Do we allow TICs for coupons/partner discounts or only applied to billed usage?
Q3: How should chargebacks be handled for customers on marketplace billing flows? Finance to advise on mapping.
dependencies: ENG-52100: Console Billing v2 list view
FIN-107: Finance approval workflow for manual refunds (process doc)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP, 4 weeks): webhook consumer + eligibility check + credit calculation engine + invoice line-item draft creation (non-destructive preview mode) + basic Console list view + unit tests.
Phase 2 (6 weeks): auto-apply credits, audit log, notifications, API read endpoints, and E2E test harness integrating with billing pipeline (staging).
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Finance overrides, manual conversion to refunds, exportable reconciliation CSV, and production rollout with monitoring dashboards.
qa_test_cases: TC1: Simulate single-tenant incident; assert TIC created, UI shows line item, invoice includes credit.
TC2: Simulate multiple-tenant incident spanning regions; assert correct tenants credited and global exposure alert fires if threshold crossed.
TC3: Override TIC in Console as Finance; assert audit log entry and API reflects adjusted value.
TC4: Reconciliation test - invoice generation consumes TICs properly and outstanding balances update accordingly.
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: 10% of customers (low-risk accounts) for first 72 hours, validate behavior and monitor costs; 50% rollout for next week; full rollout after 30 days of stable metrics.
Enable an operator kill-switch to disable automatic applies and fall back to manual ticketing if anomalies detected.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: TICs_created_per_hour, broken down by tenant and rule_id.
Alert: Global_monthly_exposure > configured_threshold => send to Finance + oncall.
Alert: Error_rate_in_credit_application > 1% for 15m => paging for infra engineer.
